description: Keeps nothing between requests that the next request depends on, so any copy can answer any request.
A server-side record that ties a session id to a user until it expires or the user logs out.
Carries the session id: the server sends `Set-Cookie` once and the browser returns it in the `Cookie` header on every request.
One store, often Redis, that every copy of the server reads and writes, so a login on one copy works on all of them.
How long a record stays valid; after it, the session is gone and a stolen id stops working.
A signed `header.payload.signature` token any server with the key can verify without a lookup; it stays valid until it expires.
Ending a credential before its expiry: deleting a session does it at once, a signed token needs a list of revoked ids.
